repository.description: Operator image repository. Built and pushed via `make build-push` in ci/private-pki-operator.

tag.description: Image tag. appVersion tracks the chart's own version, not the operator's — it is NOT a valid image tag. Set this explicitly in the consuming cluster's own values file.

installCRDs.description: Install CRDs as part of chart deployment. Set to false if CRDs are managed externally (e.g. by another tool or chart).

bindAddress.description: Address the metrics endpoint binds to. Set to "0" to disable the metrics server.

enabled.description: Create a prometheus-operator PodMonitor resource to scrape the metrics endpoint. Prometheus scrapes pods directly, so no Service is needed in front of the port.

interval.description: Scrape interval for the operator metrics endpoint. Rotations are minutes-long state machines, so a sub-minute interval buys nothing and costs samples.

port.description: Container port exposed for the metrics endpoint. Must match the port in bindAddress.

secure.description: Serve metrics over HTTPS with Kubernetes authn/authz filtering. Left false: the endpoint is reachable only from inside the cluster, and enabling it additionally requires TokenReview/SubjectAccessReview RBAC and scrape-side TLS trust, which this chart does not yet wire up.

namespace.description: Namespace for the operator itself (must be the trust-manager trust namespace).

enabled.description: Register the rotation watcher for the platform root CA. Off by default so the chart can be installed without taking ownership of a cluster's trust root; every environment enables it through its cd/ values.

reissuanceTimeout.description: Maximum time to wait for intermediate CA re-issuance before emitting a Warning.

certificateName.description: Name of the cert-manager Certificate representing the root CA.

certificateNamespace.description: Namespace of the root CA Certificate (always cert-manager for platform PKI).

name.description: Name of the cluster-scoped trust-manager Bundle resource.
Name of the staging ConfigMap the operator manages. Must NOT be the cert-manager-managed Secret — this ConfigMap is owned by the operator.

namespace.description: Namespace of the staging ConfigMap (trust-manager trust namespace).

cpu.description: CPU limit. Headroom for a rotation cascade, which walks the whole certificate tree in a burst.

memory.description: Memory limit. Deliberately close to the request: a cache that grows past this indicates the watch set has expanded unexpectedly, and failing loudly beats silently consuming the node.

cpu.description: CPU request. The operator is idle almost all the time — it reconciles on Secret and Certificate events, not on a timer — so the request is sized for scheduling rather than for throughput.

memory.description: Memory request. Sized for the informer caches, which hold Certificates and Secrets cluster-wide and dominate the footprint.

allowPrivilegeEscalation.description: Block setuid escalation. Nothing in the image is setuid, so this closes a door that is never used rather than constraining anything.

drop.description: Drop every Linux capability. This process makes API calls and nothing else; it needs none of them.

privileged.description: Never privileged. Stated explicitly rather than left to the default so the posture is auditable from values.yaml alone.

readOnlyRootFilesystem.description: Immutable root filesystem. The operator writes nothing to disk — no cache, no temp files — so a writable filesystem would only ever serve an attacker.

runAsGroup.description: GID to run as, matching the image's group.

runAsNonRoot.description: Refuse to start as UID 0. The operator needs no root capability; it reads Secrets and patches Certificates through the API server.

runAsUser.description: UID to run as. 65532 is the nonroot user baked into the distroless base image (Dockerfile: USER 65532:65532); declaring it here means the manifest asserts what the image already does rather than trusting it.

type.description: Seccomp profile. RuntimeDefault blocks the syscalls a controller never issues, which is the cheapest real reduction in kernel attack surface here.

intermediateCAConfigMap.description: ConfigMap holding the intermediate CA bundle distributed by trust-manager.

rootCAConfigMap.description: ConfigMap holding the root CA bundle distributed by trust-manager.
